reason: A worker statement interrupted mid-flight (cancellation, timeout or lost backend) leaves its SQLAlchemy connection invalidated; ExecutionSQLScope's rollback listener then read connection.info, which raised PendingRollbackError in place of the original exception. At shutdown this hit the chat follow-up poll, so the worker recorded its cleanup as failed, kept the project and every later Core shutdown or idle retirement was refused. The listener now skips invalidated connections. Selected suites cover the execution scope (new cancellation/timeout and follow-up shutdown regressions on PostgreSQL), execution workers, deployment lifecycle, orphan recovery, project handoff and admission, runtime capacity, chat acceptance, delivery, diagnostics boundaries, memory, host search, index attempts and work-batch contracts.
exclusions: Only suites that pass on pristine main are selected. test_runtime_quiescence.py, test_shutdown_readmission.py, test_chat_queue.py, test_shared_butler_memory.py, test_shared_knowledge.py, test_shared_memory_import.py and twelve other related files already fail on main (process-level suites needing a pidfd-capable interpreter, a cached model or a production UI build, plus #939 async leftovers in the chat queue); run sequentially, their failure sets are identical with and without this change. The new regressions are PostgreSQL-only because SQLite cannot hold a statement open to interrupt it. No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed. Real-Core evidence (runtime-stop after chats failing 2/2 before, 4/4 clean after) is recorded in the PR.
